correctness.rationale: The proof introduces the two spine labels and each page-label sum, yielding two exact local page inequalities and two exact global spine inequalities. Exhausting the nine spine-label cases proves weight at least 4. Equality leaves only the three spine-label patterns stated in the proof; the support rule for vertices labeled \(-1\) then forces exactly the two classified families. The binomial count follows directly. A brute-force replay for \(n=3,4,5\) and an independent page-state dynamic enumeration through \(n=12\) match the theorem.

value.rationale: Book graphs are a standard repeated-page family, and the claim gives a natural complete classification of all optimum signed-Roman labelings rather than merely recomputing a scalar. The theorem’s balance window and the sharp disappearance of the asymmetric optimum family after five pages expose a structural boundary caused by the two spine neighborhood constraints. The exact minimum-function count is a reusable enumerative invariant.
